                        description: Condition contains details for one aspect of
                          the current state of this API Resource.
                        properties:
                          lastTransitionTime:
                            description: |-
                              lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
                              This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.
                            format: date-time
                            type: string
                          message:
                            description: |-
                              message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition.
                              This may be an empty string.
                            maxLength: 32768
                            type: string
                          observedGeneration:
                            description: |-
                              observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon.
                              For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date
                              with respect to the current state of the instance.
                            format: int64
                            minimum: 0
                            type: integer
                          reason:
                            description: |-
                              reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition.
                              Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field,
                              and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API.
                              The value should be a CamelCase string.
                              This field may not be empty.
                            maxLength: 1024
                            minLength: 1
                            pattern: ^[A-Za-z]([A-Za-z0-9_,:]*[A-Za-z0-9_])?$
                            type: string
                          status:
                            description: status of the condition, one of True, False,
                              Unknown.
                            enum:
                            - "True"
                            - "False"
                            - Unknown
                            type: string
                          type:
                            description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.
                            maxLength: 316
                            pattern: ^([a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*/)?(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])$
                            type: string
                        required:
                        - lastTransitionTime
                        - message
                        - reason
                        - status
                        - type
                        type: object
                      maxItems: 8
                      type: array
                      x-kubernetes-list-map-keys:
                      - type
                      x-kubernetes-list-type: map
                    controllerName:
                      description: |-
                        ControllerName is a domain/path string that indicates the name of the controller that
                        wrote this status. This corresponds with the GatewayClass controllerName field when the
                        parentRef references a Gateway kind.

                        Example: "example.net/gateway-controller".

                        The format of this field is DOMAIN "/" PATH, where DOMAIN and PATH are valid Kubernetes names:

                         https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

                        Controllers MAY populate this field when writing status. When populating this field, controllers
                        should ensure that entries to status populated with their ControllerName are cleaned up when they
                        are no longer necessary.
                      maxLength: 253
                      minLength: 1
                      pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*\/[A-Za-z0-9\/\-._~%!$&'()*+,;=:]+$

                      description: |-
                        ParentRef is used to identify the parent resource that this status
                        is associated with. It is used to match the InferencePool with the parent
                        resource, such as a Gateway.

                        group:
                          default: gateway.networking.k8s.io
                          description: |-
                            Group is the group of the referent API object. When unspecified, the referent is assumed
                            to be in the "gateway.networking.k8s.io" API group.
                          maxLength: 253
                          minLength: 0
                          pattern: ^$|^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$
                          type: string
                        kind:
                          default: Gateway
                          description: |-
                            Kind is the kind of the referent API object. When unspecified, the referent is assumed
                            to be a "Gateway" kind.
                          maxLength: 63
                          minLength: 1
                          pattern: ^[a-zA-Z]([-a-zA-Z0-9]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$
                          type: string
                        name:
                          description: Name is the name of the referent API object.
                          maxLength: 253
                          minLength: 1
                          type: string
                        namespace:
                          description: |-
                            Namespace is the namespace of the referenced object. When unspecified, the local

                            Note that when a namespace different than the local namespace is specified,

                            namespace's owner to accept the reference. See the ReferenceGrant

                          maxLength: 63

                          pattern: ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$
                          type: string
                      required:
                      - name
                      type: object
                  required:
                  - parentRef
                  type: object
                maxItems: 32
                type: array
                x-kubernetes-list-type: atomic
            type: object
        required:
        - spec
        type: object

    storage: true

Istio/mesh configuration affecting reviews

- DestinationRule: none in bookinfo for reviews (no subsets; traffic defaults to round-robin across v1/v2/v3)
- mTLS mode at service: UNSET (inherits namespace/global policy)
- AuthorizationPolicy/PeerAuthentication/RequestAuthentication in bookinfo: none found for reviews

- Throughput: request ~1.03 KB/s avg (rising), response ~1.20 KB/s avg (rising)

- Warning events for reviews pods: none

Summary of findings

- Workload/pod logs:
  - productpage-v1 (app) logs: only normal startup; no errors.
  - istio-proxy sidecar logs: no WARN/ERROR in the recent window.
  - This strongly suggests the 500s are not coming from the application itself.

- Istio config in bookinfo:
  - Found an additional VirtualService named productpage-fault.
  - Spec shows a fault injection that aborts requests with HTTP 500 at 100%:
    - spec.hosts: [ "productpage", "productpage.bookinfo.svc.cluster.local", "productpage-bookinfo.apps-crc.testing" ]
    - spec.http[0].fault.abort.httpStatus: 500
    - spec.http[0].fault.abort.percentage.value: 100
  - Kiali also warns “More than one Virtual Service for same host.”

Most likely root cause

A fault-injection VirtualService (productpage-fault) is configured to abort 100% of requests to productpage with HTTP 500, causing all calls to productpage to return 500 before they reach the service.

Suggested fix

- Remove or disable the productpage-fault VirtualService, or set the abort percentage to 0%.
- Alternatively, scope the fault to specific matches (paths/headers) for testing only, and avoid overlapping VS for the same host.

If you want, I can remove or patch productpage-fault now.

outputSteps.content:
Here’s what I found.

Where the time is spent (from distributed traces)
- Productpage request path: productpage → details (fast, ~1–2 ms) → reviews → ratings.
- Long spans are on reviews → ratings:
  - Example trace ba4046… total ~10,023 ms: reviews → ratings call is ~10,011 ms (HTTP status_code=0 in span, indicating timeout/abort).
  - Example trace e258ee… total ~2,525 ms: reviews → ratings is ~2,502 ms (status_code=0).
- Many requests cluster around ~2.5 s, with occasional ~10 s outliers; the short (~11–14 ms) traces appear when the slow leg isn’t exercised.

Istio configs affecting this path (bookinfo namespace)
- VirtualService bookinfo
  - Hosts: *
  - Routes only the external paths to productpage. No faults or timeouts here.
- VirtualService ratings
  - Hosts: ratings.bookinfo.svc.cluster.local
  - Route: to destination subset v1
  - Fault injection: delay fixedDelay: 25s, percentage: 100 (applies to all traffic).
- DestinationRule ratings
  - Host: ratings.bookinfo.svc.cluster.local
  - Subsets: v1 (labels: version: v1)
- No VirtualService/DestinationRule found for reviews.

Correlation to latency
- Traces show the delay is specifically on the reviews → ratings leg (HTTP status_code 0 from the ratings call suggests the caller or proxy times out/aborts).
- The ratings VirtualService injects a 25-second delay for 100% of requests. Upstream components (reviews app or Envoy defaults) appear to time out before the full 25s, yielding the ~2.5 s and ~10 s end-to-end latencies observed. This exactly matches the slow spans in the traces and explains the status code 0 on the ratings call.
- No other mesh rules (e.g., for reviews) are present to explain the delay; details is consistently fast.

Most likely root cause
- An intentional fault injection on the ratings VirtualService: fixed 25s delay for all traffic to subset v1, causing upstream timeouts and driving productpage latency.

Suggested next steps
- Remove or disable the fault injection in VirtualService ratings (or set percentage: 0).
- If you still need chaos testing, limit scope (header-based matches, small percentage) and set explicit, coordinated timeouts/retries so downstream behavior is predictable.
